title: Burst jank index: session cohort comparison and cost impact
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft with notes and text-form charts from a focused bench that compares short-term burst behavior across session cohorts and quantifies the downstream cost impact. The goal was to capture a simple, operational metric ("jank index") that correlates burst-induced tail events with token-level cost overruns and SLO exposure.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- We introduce the "jank index": fraction of requests in a cohort whose 99.9th percentile latency exceeds 3x the cohort median. It is a simple burst-sensitivity signal that works on sessionized workloads.
- Small cohorts (<=100 sessions/min) show high jank in on-demand cold-start heavy configurations; large cohorts (>=1000 sessions/min) show reduced jank but higher aggregate cost due to sustained GPU spin.
- There is a non-linear cost cliff once jank index crosses ~5% for a cohort: retries + fallback + longer KV cache warmups increase per-token amortized cost by ~14-42% depending on model size and quantization.

Experiment setup (notes):
- Workload: synthetic conversation generator with variable turn lengths (mean 80 tokens, p95 320 tokens), session arrival Poisson process tuned per cohort.
- Models: rwd-7b-q4 and rwd-13b-q6 (representative open-quant variants).
- Serving modes: on-demand shared pool, prewarmed slot (session-affinity), and burst-reserve (short-lived warm slots).
- Measurement window: 60m runs, repeated 6x per config.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99/p99.9 latency (ms), successful responses, retries, KV cache hit rate, tokenized cost per request, GPU active seconds.

Definition — jank index (J):
J = (# requests where latency_99_9 > 3 * latency_median) / total_requests in cohort * 100
Intuition: flags rare but severe latency events relative to typical request latency within the cohort; easy to compute from our traces.

Cohorts tested: (session rate, session mix)
- micro: 50 sessions/min, 80% short-turn, 20% long-turn
- bursty-micro: 150 sessions/min with 20% sudden spikes (10s windows)
- steady: 800 sessions/min, stable mix
- enterprise: 2500 sessions/min, multi-tenant mix with priority scheduling

Representative numbers (rwd-7b-q4, median of 6 runs) — on-demand shared pool:
- micro: p50=48ms, p99=420ms, p99.9=1540ms, J=9.6%, cost/request=0.0014 USD
- bursty-micro: p50=56ms, p99=630ms, p99.9=2400ms, J=18.3%, cost/request=0.0019 USD
- steady: p50=52ms, p99=200ms, p99.9=780ms, J=3.1%, cost/request=0.0016 USD
- enterprise: p50=58ms, p99=190ms, p99.9=720ms, J=2.7%, cost/request=0.0021 USD

Same cohorts — prewarmed slot (session-affinity):
- micro: p50=44ms, p99=160ms, p99.9=260ms, J=0.4%, cost/request=0.0019 USD
- bursty-micro: p50=46ms, p99=210ms, p99.9=640ms, J=2.9%, cost/request=0.0022 USD
- steady: p50=45ms, p99=150ms, p99.9=300ms, J=0.2%, cost/request=0.0020 USD
- enterprise: p50=50ms, p99=140ms, p99.9=320ms, J=0.15%, cost/request=0.0026 USD

Notes on cost numbers: tokenized cost includes amortized GPU time, token generation energy estimate, and per-request control plane overhead. Prewarmed slots increase per-request baseline cost (worse for low-traffic cohorts) but truncate tail events significantly.

Text charts (ascii-style) — Jank index vs cohort (rwd-7b-q4):
Cohort        | micro   | bursty-micro | steady  | enterprise
Jank index (%) | 9.6     | 18.3         | 3.1     | 2.7

Relative cost multiplier (on-demand baseline = 1.0):
Cohort        | micro  | bursty-micro | steady | enterprise
Multiplier    | 1.00   | 1.35         | 1.14   | 1.50

Observations and interpretation:
- Bursty-micro is the worst offender: high J and a ~35% token-cost premium. Mechanism: transient cold-kv and scheduler queuing; retries amplify the visible cost.
- Prewarming converts J from double-digit down to sub-3% for low-volume cohorts, but doubles baseline cost for micro cohort; this is a clear trade-off for small customers.
- Enterprise cohort shows low J but highest per-request cost due to reserved capacity and priority lanes — acceptable given SLA.

Small-run sensitivity: rwd-13b-q6 shows similar qualitative patterns but with stronger tail amplification: same bursty-micro J jumps to ~23% and cost/request gap widens by an additional ~12% compared to 7b.

Simple decision heuristics (draft):
- If cohort session-rate < 200/min and J > 5% on on-demand, surface a recommendation: "suggest prewarm for this cohort during business hours".
- If cohort session-rate > 1000/min and J < 1%, prefer reserved capacity since aggregate cost is predictable and tail risk low.
- Introduce "burst-reserve" (short-lived warm slots billed per-second) for mid-range cohorts (200–1000/min) to minimize cost while keeping J < 3%.

Operational guidance for Console UX (proposed):
- Expose jank index per route/cohort on the routing analytics page.
- Show a toggleable cost-sensitivity overlay: if enabled, annotate routes where prewarming would reduce J by >5% and show delta cost.
- Add an "auto-apply burst-reserve" policy with a budget cap and coherence window to avoid thrashing.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Validate jank index correlation with customer-facing error tickets (CSAT) — we have a small sample mapping for 12 customers; need broader signal.
- Probe non-Poisson arrivals (weekday rush vs random) — early runs indicate weekend patterns reduce J for micro cohorts.
- Explore hybrid: partial prewarm (one slot per X sessions) vs full prewarm. What's the break-even at different token-price assumptions?

Appendix — quick trace example (abridged):
- Request A (micro cohort): p50 path, 52ms, served from cold-kv
- Request B (burst spike): queued 140ms in scheduler, then hit long GPU spin due to contiguous larger requests -> p99.9=2400ms -> user retry -> two extra requests -> net cost multiplier x1.8

Next steps (owner action items):
- Run a targeted A/B comparing partial-prewarm (1 slot per 300 sessions) vs full-prewarm for 2 models across 3 geos (owner: Marcus).
- Add jank index to daily micro-dashboard (owner: Aisha).
- Open an internal experiment ticket to evaluate burst-reserve billing semantics (owner: Diego).

Conversation notes / rough links: see linked_artifacts for pointers to the experiment ticket, a Confluence explainer, and the slack thread where we debated prewarm price assumptions.

-- End of draft --

Notes to reader: this doc is intentionally colloquial / bench-notebook style. Numbers are median-of-repeats and should be treated as directional. Feedback welcome; if you want the raw traces or the bench harness, ping me and I'll push the dataset and the runner config to the OBS S3 bucket.
